title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第23部分：每一种感官都是词元

chapters.History: 1. 我们是怎么走到这里的
chapters.Unigram: 3. 给每一种切法一个概率

57fec6823d05.en: A transformer reads a sequence of tokens. So how does a model look at a picture, or listen to a voice? <bookmark mark='a'/> Everything is turned into tokens first: text into pieces of words, a picture into codes for its patches, sound into codes for slices of time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then it's all one sequence, and one model can read it, and write it.
57fec6823d05.zh: Transformer读的是一串词元。那么，模型怎么看一张图片，怎么听一段声音？<bookmark mark='a'/>先把一切都变成词元：文字变成词的片段，图片变成各个小块的编码，声音变成一段段时间的编码。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后它们就是同一个序列，一个模型就能读它，也能写它。

d64e593ee507.en: Every sense poses the same questions. What should a token be? How many does a sentence, a picture or a second of speech need? And how are the codes learned? <bookmark mark='a'/> We'll follow seventy years of answers: a machine that recognized ten spoken digits in 1952, the statistical recognizers that followed, byte-pair encoding, CTC, WaveNet, CLIP and Whisper, up to models that listen while they speak. <bookmark mark='b'/> And we'll build small versions on the computer making this video: tokenizers, codebooks, a speech codec, a speech recognizer, and a model that matches pictures with captions.
d64e593ee507.zh: 每一种感官都提出同样的问题。一个词元应该是什么？一句话、一张图、一秒钟的语音，各需要多少个？这些编码又是怎么学出来的？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会沿着七十年的答案走一遍：1952年一台能听懂十个数字的机器，随后的统计式识别器，字节对编码，CTC，WaveNet，CLIP和Whisper，一直到边听边说的模型。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们还会在制作这段视频的电脑上，搭出它们的小版本：分词器，码本，一个语音编解码器，一个语音识别器，还有一个给图片配说明文字的模型。

692ac59d9c7c.en: This is Part 23 of AI, Built. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: tokenizers for text, and what a token is worth in bits; vector quantization, its codebooks and how they fail; sampling, spectra and neural audio codecs; listening, from templates to CTC and Whisper; speaking, up to the model narrating this video; and matching pictures with words, from CLIP to models that see, hear and talk.
692ac59d9c7c.zh: 这是《人工智能，从零搭建》的第23部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分讲：文本的分词器，以及一个词元值多少比特；向量量化、它的码本，以及码本怎样失效；采样、频谱和神经音频编解码器；听，从模板到CTC和Whisper；说，一直讲到为这段视频配音的模型；还有让图片和文字配对，从CLIP一直到能看、能听、能说的模型。

79554faf59d2.en: Chapter one. How we got here.
79554faf59d2.zh: 第1章。我们是怎么走到这里的。

9e4f17ac5db6.en: Machines were listening long before they could read. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1952 Bell Labs built Audrey, a rack of electronics that recognized the ten digits spoken by one person, ninety-seven to ninety-nine times in a hundred. <bookmark mark='b'/> In the 1970s recognizers learned to stretch time to match a template, and then, at IBM and Carnegie Mellon, to treat speech as a hidden Markov model, Part 7's statistics, which ruled for thirty years. <bookmark mark='c'/> Neural networks took over the sound model in 2012, and in 2022 Whisper transcribed nearly a hundred languages. <bookmark mark='d'/> Speaking went the same way: from the Voder, played on a keyboard at the 1939 World's Fair, to formant synthesizers and spliced recordings, and in 2016 to WaveNet, a network that writes sound one sample at a time.
9e4f17ac5db6.zh: 机器会听，比会读早得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>1952年，贝尔实验室造出了Audrey，一架电子设备，能听懂一个人说的十个数字，一百次里对九十七到九十九次。<bookmark mark='b'/>到了1970年代，识别器学会了拉伸时间去对齐模板；接着，在IBM和卡内基梅隆大学，人们把语音当成隐马尔可夫模型来处理，也就是第7部分的统计方法，它统治了三十年。<bookmark mark='c'/>2012年，神经网络接管了声音模型；2022年，Whisper能转写将近一百种语言。<bookmark mark='d'/>说话这条线也一样：从1939年世界博览会上用键盘弹出来的Voder，到共振峰合成器和拼接录音，再到2016年的WaveNet，一个一次写一个采样点的网络。

af44cb68e960.en: Then speech became language modeling: Tacotron, then in 2023 VALL-E, which writes a voice as codes the way a language model writes words. <bookmark mark='a'/> Text needed units of its own. Word models choked on words they had never seen, and characters made sequences long. In 1994 Philip Gage published a way to compress files by replacing common pairs of bytes; in 2016 it became the standard way to cut text into tokens, and versions over bytes and over probabilities followed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pictures met words around 2014, when networks learned to caption photographs; in 2021 CLIP learned from four hundred million captioned pictures off the web, and by 2023 a vision encoder bolted onto a language model could talk about an image.
af44cb68e960.zh: 接着，语音合成变成了语言建模：先是Tacotron，然后是2023年的VALL-E，它像语言模型写词那样，把一个人的声音写成编码。<bookmark mark='a'/>文本需要自己的单位。以词为单位的模型，碰到没见过的词就卡住；以字符为单位，序列又太长。1994年，菲利普·盖奇发表了一种压缩文件的方法：反复替换最常见的字节对；2016年，它成了把文本切成词元的标准做法，后来又出现了基于字节、基于概率的版本。<bookmark mark='b'/>图片和文字在2014年前后相遇，那时网络学会了给照片配说明；2021年，CLIP从网上四亿张带说明的图片里学习；到2023年，把一个视觉编码器接到语言模型上，它就能谈论一张图片了。

d0efe1dcc6b5.en: <bookmark mark='a'/> In the last few years the threads met. Once speech, pictures and text are all tokens, one transformer can read and write them all: GPT-4o in 2024, Moshi, Qwen's omni models. <bookmark mark='b'/> This part builds that idea from the bottom up: what a token is and what it is worth, how codes are learned, how sound and pictures become sequences, and how the senses are matched.
d0efe1dcc6b5.zh: <bookmark mark='a'/>最近几年，这几条线汇到了一起。一旦语音、图片和文字都成了词元，一个Transformer就能把它们全部读写：2024年的GPT-4o，Moshi，还有通义千问的全模态模型。<bookmark mark='b'/>这一部分从底层把这个想法搭起来：词元是什么、值多少，编码怎样学出来，声音和图片怎样变成序列，各种感官又怎样配对。

c5ad2bde06e8.en: A tokenizer decides what a model's units are. Whole words? <bookmark mark='a'/> In two million characters of our novels there are 21,374 different words, and still 5.3 percent of the words in the scoreboard's passage never appear among them. A model of words has nothing to say about those. <bookmark mark='b'/> Single characters never run out, but a sentence becomes a long sequence, and attention's cost grows with the square of its length. Byte-pair encoding finds the units in between.
c5ad2bde06e8.zh: 分词器决定模型的基本单位是什么。用整个词吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>在我们小说里的两百万个字符中，有21374个不同的词，可测试段落里仍有5.3%的词从没出现过。一个以词为单位的模型，对这些词无话可说。<bookmark mark='b'/>单个字符永远不会不够用，但一句话会变成一个很长的序列，而注意力的代价随长度的平方增长。字节对编码找的是介于两者之间的单位。

b41869c66f81.en: In 1994 Philip Gage described a way to compress a file: find the pair of bytes that occurs most often, replace it everywhere with one new symbol, and repeat. In 2016 Rico Sennrich, Barry Haddow and Alexandra Birch used it to cut words for machine translation. Start from single characters, merge the commonest neighbouring pair, and repeat. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are the first merges on our novels: a space and a t, h and e, then the starts and ends of words, and soon whole words. Each new symbol is a token.
b41869c66f81.zh: 1994年，菲利普·盖奇描述了一种压缩文件的方法：找出出现最频繁的字节对，把它处处换成一个新符号，然后重复。2016年，里科·森里希、巴里·哈多和亚历山德拉·伯奇用它来为机器翻译切分词语。从单个字符出发，合并最常见的相邻对，然后重复。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是在我们小说上学到的头几次合并：先是空格和t，h和e，然后是词的开头和结尾，很快就是整个词。每个新符号就是一个词元。

6dfaaa8fe697.en: Why is this compression? <bookmark mark='a'/> Each time the merged pair occurs, two symbols become one, so a merge that applies n times shortens the text by exactly n. <bookmark mark='b'/> After k merges the text is its original length minus the sum of the counts, <bookmark mark='c'/> and choosing the commonest pair means taking the biggest saving next: a greedy compressor. <bookmark mark='d'/> On our novels the first merge alone saves 48,515 symbols, and after 8,000 merges the text is 23 percent of its length in characters. The savings shrink as the merges get rarer.
6dfaaa8fe697.zh: 这为什么是压缩？<bookmark mark='a'/>被合并的那一对每出现一次，两个符号就变成一个，所以一次用上n次的合并，正好让文本缩短n个符号。<bookmark mark='b'/>合并k次之后，文本长度就是原来的长度减去这些次数的总和，<bookmark mark='c'/>而挑最常见的一对，就是每次都先拿最大的节省：一个贪心的压缩器。<bookmark mark='d'/>在我们的小说上，光是第一次合并就省下48515个符号；合并8000次之后，文本长度只剩按字符算的23%。合并越往后越罕见，省下的也越来越少。

904852cf6a22.en: The more merges, the bigger the tokens. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's one sentence, cut into characters, then after 500, 2,000 and 8,000 merges. <bookmark mark='b'/> With 8,000 merges a token covers 3.9 characters of the passage on average, so a transformer sees the same text in a fraction of the steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> BERT's tokenizer, WordPiece, merges by a different rule: the pair whose parts rarely occur apart, the merge that most raises the text's likelihood. Its first merges on our novels are rare pairs that always come together. <bookmark mark='d'/> Real vocabularies run from fifty thousand tokens in GPT-2 to over a quarter of a million in Gemma 3.
904852cf6a22.zh: 合并越多，词元越大。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是同一句话，先切成字符，再看合并500次、2000次和8000次之后的样子。<bookmark mark='b'/>合并8000次时，一个词元平均覆盖测试段落的3.9个字符，所以Transformer只用几分之一的步数就读完同样的文本。<bookmark mark='c'/>BERT的分词器WordPiece按另一条规则合并：挑那些组成部分很少分开出现的对，也就是最能提高文本似然的合并。它在我们小说上的头几次合并，都是总是一起出现的罕见组合。<bookmark mark='d'/>真实的词表，从GPT-2的五万个词元，到Gemma 3的超过二十五万个。

02ca22c2d181.en: Chapter three. A probability for every cut.
02ca22c2d181.zh: 第3章。给每一种切法一个概率。

eef98708d73a.en: Byte-pair encoding cuts each word one way, fixed by the order of its merges. In 2018 Taku Kudo proposed a model instead. <bookmark mark='a'/> A vocabulary of pieces, each with a probability. A cut of a word into pieces scores the product of their probabilities, and the word's probability is the sum over every cut. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are a few ways to write armchair with the pieces our model learned. <bookmark mark='c'/> The tokenizer keeps the most probable cut.
eef98708d73a.zh: 字节对编码对每个词只有一种切法，由合并的顺序决定。2018年，工藤拓提出改用一个模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个片段组成的词表，每个片段有一个概率。把一个词切成若干片段，这种切法的得分是各片段概率的乘积，而这个词的概率是所有切法之和。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是用我们的模型学到的片段，写出armchair的几种方式。<bookmark mark='c'/>分词器保留概率最大的那种切法。

ab617a0142ec.en: Every cut of a word is a path through a lattice. <bookmark mark='a'/> Put a node between each pair of letters, and an arc for every piece in the vocabulary. A cut is a path from the first node to the last. <bookmark mark='b'/> The sum over all cuts is computed left to right: the probability of reaching node j adds up every arc that ends there, from every earlier node, the forward algorithm of Part 7's hidden Markov models. <bookmark mark='c'/> Replace the sum with a maximum and you get the best cut. <bookmark mark='d'/> Run it backward as well, and you get how often each piece is expected to be used: what training needs.
ab617a0142ec.zh: 一个词的每一种切法，都是一张格上的一条路径。<bookmark mark='a'/>在每两个字母之间放一个节点，词表里的每个片段画一条弧。一种切法，就是从第一个节点走到最后一个节点的一条路径。<bookmark mark='b'/>所有切法之和可以从左往右算：到达节点j的概率，是所有终止在那里的弧之和，来自之前的每一个节点，这正是第7部分隐马尔可夫模型的前向算法。<bookmark mark='c'/>把求和换成取最大，就得到最好的切法。<bookmark mark='d'/>再从右往左算一遍，就得到每个片段预计会被用到几次：训练正需要这个。

8020fd282ec1.en: Training starts from far too many pieces: the most frequent substrings of the text, 27,517 of them after the first round. <bookmark mark='a'/> Then expectation-maximization, Part 7's EM: compute how often each piece is expected to be used, summed over every cut of every word, and set each probability in proportion. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then prune: for each piece, measure how much the likelihood would fall without it, keep the three quarters that matter most and every single letter, and repeat. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here is the model's own measure of the novels, in bits per character, as the vocabulary shrinks: smaller vocabularies cost bits, 0.55 of them from the first round down to 4,096 pieces.
8020fd282ec1.zh: 训练从多得多的片段开始：文本里最常见的子串，第一轮之后有27517个。<bookmark mark='a'/>然后是期望最大化，第7部分的EM：对每个词的每一种切法求和，算出每个片段预计被用到几次，再按比例设定它的概率。<bookmark mark='b'/>接着剪枝：对每个片段，算一算没有它时似然会下降多少，保留最重要的四分之三，以及每一个单字母，然后重复。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是模型自己对小说的度量，以每字符比特数计，随着词表缩小而变化：词表越小，代价越多，从第一轮到4096个片段，一共多了0.55比特。

8ac17dd2460b.en: How different are the two? <bookmark mark='a'/> At 4,096 pieces each, on the scoreboard's passage, BPE's tokens are a little longer: 3.54 characters a token for BPE, 3.46 for the unigram model, and 15 percent of the words are cut differently. <bookmark mark='b'/> The unigram model can also sample cuts instead of taking the best, so a model in training sees the same word written several ways; Kudo called it subword regularization. <bookmark mark='c'/> His SentencePiece library runs either method on raw text, with the space as just another symbol, and it cut the text for T5, the first two Llamas and Gemma.
8ac17dd2460b.zh: 两者差别有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>各用4096个片段，在测试段落上，BPE的词元稍长一些：BPE每个词元3.54个字符，一元模型3.46个，有15%的词切法不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>一元模型还可以随机采样切法，而不总取最好的，这样训练中的模型会看到同一个词的好几种写法；工藤拓称之为子词正则化。<bookmark mark='c'/>他的SentencePiece库能在原始文本上运行这两种方法，把空格也当作一个普通符号，T5、前两代Llama和Gemma都用它来切分文本。

7ff624801282.en: Chapter four. What a token is worth.

c69b86f2a967.en: A tokenizer changes what a model has to guess. A model that predicts bigger tokens has more to guess each time, so its bits per token can't be compared with a byte model's. <bookmark mark='a'/> The fair currency is Part 1's bits per character: the text's total surprise, divided by its length. <bookmark mark='b'/> Divide the top and the bottom by the number of tokens, <bookmark mark='c'/> and bits per character is bits per token divided by characters per token. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our 4,096-piece BPE model pays 8.36 bits for a token of the scoreboard's passage, and a token covers 3.54 characters: 2.36 bits per character.
c69b86f2a967.zh: 分词器改变了模型要猜的东西。预测大词元的模型，每次要猜的更多，所以它的每词元比特数没法和字节模型相比。<bookmark mark='a'/>公平的货币是第1部分的每字符比特数：文本的总意外度，除以它的长度。<bookmark mark='b'/>分子分母同时除以词元数，<bookmark mark='c'/>每字符比特数就等于每词元比特数除以每词元字符数。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们4096个片段的BPE模型，在测试段落上每个词元花8.36比特，一个词元覆盖3.54个字符：每字符2.36比特。

39359d3a4cec.en: Now a fair race. Five tokenizers: raw bytes, and BPE and the unigram model with 1,024 and with 4,096 pieces. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each gets the same small transformer and the same budget of arithmetic, three seeds each. <bookmark mark='b'/> A bigger vocabulary makes every token dearer, because the output layer grows with it, so those models take fewer steps. But each of their tokens carries more text: in its budget the 4,096-piece BPE model reads 3.6 million characters, the byte model 2.0 million.
39359d3a4cec.zh: 现在来一场公平的比赛。五种分词器：原始字节，以及各用1024个和4096个片段的BPE和一元模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一种都用同样的小Transformer，同样的计算预算，各跑三个种子。<bookmark mark='b'/>词表越大，每个词元越贵，因为输出层随词表增大，所以这些模型走的步数更少。但它们的每个词元携带的文本更多：在预算之内，4096个片段的BPE模型读了3.6百万个字符，字节模型读了2.0百万个。

48ff4e8a447a.en: Here they learn, all fifteen runs, measured in bits per character on held-out text as the budget is spent. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the scoreboard's passage, the unigram model with 1,024 pieces does best, at 2.26 bits per character, and raw bytes does worst, at 2.46; the seeds never differ by more than 0.05. <bookmark mark='b'/> the unigram model beats BPE at 1,024 pieces, and the unigram model beats BPE at 4,096 pieces.
48ff4e8a447a.zh: 这是它们学习的过程，全部十五次训练，随着预算的消耗，在留出文本上以每字符比特数衡量。<bookmark mark='a'/>在测试段落上，1024个片段的一元模型最好，每字符2.26比特；原始字节最差，2.46比特；不同种子之间相差从不超过0.05。<bookmark mark='b'/>在1024个片段时，一元模型胜过BPE；在4096个片段时，一元模型胜过BPE。

4adc1c7a284d.en: Why does the tokenizer matter at all? <bookmark mark='a'/> With bigger tokens, every FLOP buys more text, and the same window of 128 tokens holds more of the passage. <bookmark mark='b'/> But a bigger vocabulary means a bigger output layer, and rarer tokens, each seen fewer times in training. <bookmark mark='c'/> In a model with billions of parameters the output layer is a small part of the cost, which is why real vocabularies have a hundred thousand tokens or more. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here is what two of ours write after the passage's opening words, at a temperature of 0.8. The tokenizer is a hidden choice behind every score, and bits per character keeps the comparison honest.
4adc1c7a284d.zh: 分词器到底为什么重要？<bookmark mark='a'/>词元越大，每一次浮点运算买到的文本越多，同样128个词元的窗口，装下的段落也越多。<bookmark mark='b'/>但词表越大，输出层越大，词元也越罕见，每个在训练中出现的次数越少。<bookmark mark='c'/>在有几十亿参数的模型里，输出层只占代价的一小部分，所以真实的词表有十万个词元甚至更多。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是我们的两个模型在段落开头几个词之后写出的东西，温度0.8。分词器是每个分数背后的一个隐藏选择，而每字符比特数让比较保持诚实。

193fe5280579.en: Tokenizers fail in their own ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> A character the vocabulary never saw becomes unknown. Letters hidden inside one token are hard to count or spell. And a vocabulary learned mostly on English cuts other languages into more tokens, so they cost more. <bookmark mark='b'/> GPT-2's fix, in 2019, was to run BPE on bytes. Any text is a sequence of bytes in UTF-8, one to four per character, with only 256 possible values, so with the bytes as the starting alphabet nothing is ever unknown.<bookmark mark='c'/> The series' own language model, the one Parts 18 to 30 train and probe, uses a byte-level BPE with 4,096 tokens; on the passage it averages 3.23 characters a token.
193fe5280579.zh: 分词器有自己的失败方式。<bookmark mark='a'/>词表没见过的字符会变成未知。藏在一个词元里的字母，很难数清、很难拼写。而一个主要在英语上学出来的词表，会把其他语言切成更多的词元，于是它们花费更多。<bookmark mark='b'/>GPT-2在2019年的办法，是在字节上做BPE。任何文本在UTF-8里都是一串字节，每个字符一到四个字节，只有256种可能的取值，所以以字节为起始字母表，就永远不会有未知。<bookmark mark='c'/>本系列自己的语言模型，也就是第18到30部分训练和剖析的那个，用的是一个有4096个词元的字节级BPE；在测试段落上，平均每个词元3.23个字符。

2aa3b7ebf20b.en: Could a model skip the tokenizer and read bytes? <bookmark mark='a'/> Google's ByT5, in 2021, did exactly that, at the price of sequences several times longer than BPE's. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2023 Meta's MegaByte grouped the bytes into fixed patches: a big transformer looks at the patches, and a small one writes the bytes inside each. <bookmark mark='c'/> But a fixed patch spends as much on the end of a predictable word as on its surprising start. In December 2024 Meta's Byte Latent Transformer let the data decide: a small byte model reads ahead, and a new patch starts wherever it is unsure of the next byte. Here, the same 37 bytes become 10 fixed patches or 11 entropy patches.
2aa3b7ebf20b.zh: 模型能不能跳过分词器，直接读字节？<bookmark mark='a'/>谷歌的ByT5在2021年就这么做了，代价是序列比BPE长好几倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>2023年，Meta的MegaByte把字节分成固定大小的块：一个大Transformer看这些块，一个小Transformer写出每块里的字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>但固定的块，在一个可预测的词尾上花的力气，和在出人意料的词首上一样多。2024年12月，Meta的字节潜变量Transformer让数据自己决定：一个小的字节模型先往前读，哪里对下一个字节没把握，哪里就开始一个新块。这里，同样的37个字节，变成10个固定块，或者11个按熵划分的块。

bc1efc040e8a.en: Here is that idea on our own byte model, the byte-level transformer from chapter four, reading a line of the passage. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each bar is how unsure the model is about the next byte: its entropy, in bits. The dots are how surprised it was by the byte that actually came. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the start of a word the next letter is wide open; inside a word, after a few letters, the rest is almost certain. <bookmark mark='c'/> Start a new patch wherever the entropy crosses a threshold, and the patches follow the information: short where the text is surprising, long where it is predictable.
bc1efc040e8a.zh: 这是这个想法在我们自己的字节模型上的样子，也就是第4章的字节级Transformer，读测试段落中的一行。<bookmark mark='a'/>每根柱子是模型对下一个字节有多没把握：它的熵，以比特计。点是它对实际出现的那个字节有多意外。<bookmark mark='b'/>在一个词的开头，下一个字母完全开放；在词的中间，读过几个字母之后，剩下的几乎已经确定。<bookmark mark='c'/>只要熵越过一个阈值，就开始一个新块，这些块就会跟着信息走：文本出人意料的地方块短，可预测的地方块长。

50272122a2e9.en: How well do the patches follow the surprise? Sweep the threshold, and for each, measure the average patch length and the share of the model's total surprise that falls on the first byte of a patch. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the threshold where patches are as long as our BPE tokens, 3.54 bytes on average, 28 percent of the bytes start a patch, and they carry 46 percent of the surprise. <bookmark mark='b'/> BPE's token starts, about as many, carry 24 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is the case for patches: spend the big model's steps where the information is. Meta's study found byte patches matching a tokenized model of the same compute, up to 8 billion parameters.
50272122a2e9.zh: 这些块跟意外度跟得有多紧？扫一遍阈值，对每个阈值，量出平均块长，以及模型的总意外度中，落在块的第一个字节上的比例。<bookmark mark='a'/>当块的平均长度和我们的BPE词元一样，都是3.54个字节时，28%的字节是块的开头，它们承担了46%的意外度。<bookmark mark='b'/>BPE词元的开头，数量差不多，只承担24%。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是分块的理由：把大模型的步数花在信息所在的地方。Meta的研究发现，在同样的计算量下，字节分块的模型能赶上用分词器的模型，一直到80亿参数。

63c954cc7f06.en: Text comes in pieces; pictures and sound are continuous. To make tokens of them we need a vocabulary of shapes: a codebook. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cut every letter picture into four by four patches and find sixteen typical ones by k-means: <bookmark mark='k'/> start with sixteen guesses, give each patch to its nearest guess, move each guess to the average of its patches, and repeat. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now a picture is a sequence of numbers from zero to fifteen: each patch is replaced by its nearest code. <bookmark mark='c'/> With more codes the copy comes closer; the numbers are the error per pixel, on held-out patches, for 16, 64, 256 and 1,024 codes.
63c954cc7f06.zh: 文本本来就是一块一块的；图片和声音却是连续的。要把它们变成词元，我们需要一个形状的词汇表：一本码本。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每张字母图片切成四乘四的小块，用k均值找出十六个典型的小块：<bookmark mark='k'/>先随便猜十六个，把每个小块分给离它最近的猜测，再把每个猜测移到分给它的小块的平均处，然后重复。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在一张图片就是一串0到15的数字：每个小块换成离它最近的码。<bookmark mark='c'/>码越多，复制品越接近原图；这些数字是留出小块上每个像素的误差，分别对应16, 64, 256和1024个码。

13cfc200fda9.en: In a real model the codebook is learned with the encoder and decoder, as in Part 20's VQ-VAE, and that hits a snag. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each encoder output z is replaced by its nearest code. Picking the nearest is a jump, with no gradient. <bookmark mark='b'/> The fix is the straight-through trick: forward, use the code; backward, pretend nothing happened, and hand the code's gradient straight to z. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two more terms keep things together: one pulls each chosen code toward the outputs that chose it; the other, the commitment loss, weighted by beta, keeps each output near the code it was snapped to. <bookmark mark='d'/> And here is the weakness: a code that nobody picks gets no gradient at all. It never moves, and it is never picked.
13cfc200fda9.zh: 在真正的模型里，码本是和编码器、解码器一起学出来的，就像第20部分的VQ-VAE，而这会遇到一个难题。<bookmark mark='a'/>编码器的每个输出z，都被换成离它最近的码。挑最近的，是一次跳跃，没有梯度。<bookmark mark='b'/>解决办法是直通技巧：前向时用码；反向时假装什么都没发生，把码上的梯度直接交给z。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有两项把它们拴在一起：一项把每个被选中的码拉向选它的那些输出；另一项是承诺损失，乘以β，让每个输出靠近它被吸附到的码。<bookmark mark='d'/>而弱点就在这里：没人选的码，一点梯度也得不到。它永远不动，也永远不会被选中。

51adfcc27018.en: We trained a small VQ autoencoder on the letters: each letter becomes a five by five grid of codes from a book of 256, the same budget of 1,500 steps and three seeds for every variant. <bookmark mark='a'/> With the textbook recipe, the codebook collapses: at the end only 86 of the 256 codes are in use on held-out letters, on average over the seeds. <bookmark mark='b'/> A popular repair updates each code as a running average of the outputs that chose it, an exponential moving average, which is k-means done online. Here EMA alone does not fix it: 76 codes in use. <bookmark mark='c'/> What works is to start the codes on real encoder outputs and restart any code unused for fifty steps at a random output of the batch: 255 codes in use.
51adfcc27018.zh: 我们在字母上训练了一个小的VQ自编码器：每个字母变成一个五乘五的码网格，码本有256个码；每种方法都用同样的1500步预算，三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>按教科书的做法，码本坍缩了：到最后，256个码里只有86个在用，这是在留出字母上、对三个种子的平均。<bookmark mark='b'/>一种流行的修补，是把每个码更新为选它的那些输出的滑动平均，即指数移动平均，相当于在线的k均值。这里光靠EMA解决不了：76个码在用。<bookmark mark='c'/>管用的办法是让码从真实的编码器输出开始，并把五十步没被用到的码，重启到这一批里一个随机的输出上：255个码在用。

019cafc2631f.en: A fairer measure than counting codes is perplexity: the number of equally used codes that would carry the same information. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plain VQ reaches 67, EMA 56, and EMA with restarts 194. <bookmark mark='b'/> The reconstructions: EMA with restarts rebuilds the held-out letters best, at 4.6 thousandths per pixel. <bookmark mark='c'/> Restarts are standard in audio codecs; the other cure is to get rid of the learned codebook altogether, the subject of the next chapter.
019cafc2631f.zh: 比数码更公平的度量是困惑度：携带同样信息量所需的、被均匀使用的码的个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>普通VQ达到67，EMA是56，带重启的EMA是194。<bookmark mark='b'/>再看重建：带重启的EMA把留出字母重建得最好，每个像素误差千分之4.6。<bookmark mark='c'/>重启在音频编解码器里是标准做法；另一种治法是干脆不要学出来的码本，这是下一章的主题。

4af23e2ad605.en: Chapter seven. Codes without a codebook.

af66736ff47e.en: In 2023 Fabian Mentzer and colleagues at Google asked whether the codebook needs learning at all. <bookmark mark='a'/> Finite scalar quantization: map the encoder's output to a few numbers, squash each into a fixed range, and round it to one of a few levels. <bookmark mark='b'/> The codebook is just the grid of all the combinations: with four numbers of four levels each, 256 codes, eight bits, the same as our VQ. <bookmark mark='c'/> Rounding has no gradient either, so the straight-through trick again. But there is nothing to collapse: no code can be stranded, because no code is learned.
af66736ff47e.zh: 2023年，谷歌的法比安·门策尔和同事问：码本到底需不需要学？<bookmark mark='a'/>有限标量量化：把编码器的输出映射成几个数，把每个数压进一个固定范围，再四舍五入到几个等级之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>码本就是所有组合构成的网格：四个数、每个四级，就是256个码，八比特，和我们的VQ一样。<bookmark mark='c'/>四舍五入同样没有梯度，所以还是用直通技巧。但没有什么可坍缩的：没有码会被搁浅，因为没有码是学出来的。

5c92d6aa929b.en: Months later, Lijun Yu and colleagues pushed it to the limit for their video tokenizer, MAGVIT-v2: lookup-free quantization. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep only each number's sign. With d numbers there are two to the d codes, the corners of a cube, and a vocabulary of a quarter of a million costs no table at all. <bookmark mark='b'/> To make the codes earn their keep they add an entropy term: each output should be confidently near one corner, while across the batch all the corners are used.
5c92d6aa929b.zh: 几个月后，于立军和同事在他们的视频分词器MAGVIT-v2里把它推到了极致：免查表量化。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个数只保留正负号。d个数就有2的d次方个码，也就是一个立方体的各个角，一个二十五万的词表根本不需要表。<bookmark mark='b'/>为了让这些码物尽其用，他们加了一个熵项：每个输出都要有把握地靠近某一个角，而在整批数据里，所有角都要被用到。

a6600a44894d.en: All five, at 256 codes, the same network, the same steps and three seeds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Perplexity: 121 for FSQ, 60 for LFQ, 67 for plain VQ. FSQ uses its grid better than plain VQ uses its codebook; LFQ, at its paper's entropy weight, does not. <bookmark mark='b'/> On error, EMA with restarts comes first at 4.6 thousandths, then FSQ at 5.3, and LFQ last at 15.0. The Google team's point was not that FSQ wins outright, but that it matches VQ without any of VQ's repairs.
a6600a44894d.zh: 五种方法，都是256个码，同样的网络、同样的步数、三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>困惑度：FSQ是121，LFQ是60，普通VQ是67。FSQ用它的网格，比普通VQ用它的码本更充分；LFQ在论文的熵权重下则不然。<bookmark mark='b'/>论误差，带重启的EMA第一，千分之4.6；其次是FSQ，千分之5.3；LFQ最后，千分之15.0。谷歌团队的论点不是FSQ全面胜出，而是它不需要VQ的任何修补就能和VQ相当。

b95d6a0acc12.en: One more trick, the one sound codecs rely on: quantize in stages. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first stage codes the patch roughly; the second codes what the first missed; then a third, and a fourth. The patch is rebuilt as the sum. <bookmark mark='b'/> Is it better than one big codebook? Not at equal bits. At eight bits one codebook of 256 codes, error 0.083, beats two stages of 16, 0.117. <bookmark mark='c'/> But residual stages keep going where one codebook can't: sixteen bits would need a table of 65,536 entries, and four stages of 16 reach 0.083 with 64. That is residual vector quantization, inside nearly every neural audio codec.
b95d6a0acc12.zh: 还有一个技巧，声音编解码器都靠它：分级量化。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一级粗略地编码这个小块；第二级编码第一级漏掉的部分；然后第三级、第四级。小块被重建为它们的和。<bookmark mark='b'/>它比一本大码本更好吗？在比特数相同时不是。在八比特时，一本256个码的码本，误差0.083，胜过两级、每级16个码的0.117。<bookmark mark='c'/>但残差的各级能一直往下走，而单一码本跟不上：十六比特需要一张65536项的表，而四级、每级16个码，只用64项就达到0.083。这就是残差向量量化，几乎每个神经音频编解码器里都有它。

7f2d11b4fd60.en: A microphone measures air pressure, and a computer keeps a sample of it at regular ticks. How fast is fast enough? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a pure tone of frequency f, sampled f s times a second. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add f s to the frequency, and at every sample the phase gains a whole number of turns, so the samples don't change at all. <bookmark mark='c'/> And because cosine is even, f s minus f gives the same samples as f. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the samples can only tell apart frequencies between zero and half the sampling rate. A seven kilohertz tone sampled eight thousand times a second lands exactly on a one kilohertz tone. The converse is the sampling theorem of Nyquist and Shannon: a signal with nothing above half the rate is fixed exactly by its samples.
7f2d11b4fd60.zh: 麦克风测的是气压，而计算机按固定的节拍保留它的样本。多快才够快？<bookmark mark='a'/>取一个频率为f的纯音，每秒采样f_s次。<bookmark mark='b'/>把频率加上f_s，每个采样点的相位都多转了整数圈，所以样本完全不变。<bookmark mark='c'/>而因为余弦是偶函数，f_s减f给出的样本和f一样。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以样本只能分辨零到采样率一半之间的频率。一个七千赫的音调，每秒采样八千次，恰好落在一个一千赫的音调上。反过来就是奈奎斯特和香农的采样定理：一个不含采样率一半以上成分的信号，完全由它的样本决定。

633d33b4b485.en: We can check it numerically. <bookmark mark='a'/> Sample tones of one, three, five and seven kilohertz eight thousand times a second, and find the peak of each one's spectrum: 1.00, 3.00, 3.00, 1.00 kilohertz. <bookmark mark='b'/> Above four kilohertz, every frequency folds back into the band below, a zigzag: aliasing.
633d33b4b485.zh: 我们可以用数值验证。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一千、三千、五千和七千赫的音调各以每秒八千次采样，找出各自频谱的峰：1.00, 3.00, 3.00, 1.00千赫。<bookmark mark='b'/>四千赫以上的每个频率，都折回到下面的频段里，形成一条锯齿：这就是混叠。

fd1bccfe9aac.en: Speech shows why this matters. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this sentence from a held-out Kokoro voice, 4 percent of the energy lies above two kilohertz. <bookmark mark='b'/> Keep every fourth sample, four thousand a second, and that energy doesn't vanish; it folds down into the band that's left: by our measure, 5 percent of what remains below two kilohertz is folded energy. <bookmark mark='c'/> Filter first, then keep every fourth, and the band below two kilohertz is clean. <bookmark mark='d'/> So every sampling rate is a decision about what to keep: eight kilohertz for the telephone, sixteen for Whisper, twenty-four for most audio codecs.
fd1bccfe9aac.zh: 语音说明了这为什么重要。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一个留出的Kokoro声音说的这句话里，4%的能量在两千赫以上。<bookmark mark='b'/>每四个样本只留一个，也就是每秒四千个，这部分能量并不会消失，而是折到剩下的频段里：按我们的度量，两千赫以下剩下的部分里，有5%是折进来的能量。<bookmark mark='c'/>先滤波，再每四个留一个，两千赫以下的频段就是干净的。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以每个采样率都是一个取舍：电话用八千赫，Whisper用一万六千赫，大多数音频编解码器用两万四千赫。

8d2b7a66ca50.en: A wave is hard to read, so speech models look at its spectrum, slice by slice. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cut the signal into windows of 25 milliseconds, one every 10, taper each with a Hann window and take its Fourier transform: the short-time Fourier transform, a picture of frequency against time. <bookmark mark='b'/> The ear hears pitch roughly by ratios, so the frequencies are pooled into bands evenly spaced on the mel scale: narrow below a kilohertz, wider above. <bookmark mark='c'/> Take the logarithm of each band's energy, keep the top eight decades, and you have exactly what Whisper hears: 80 log-mel bands every 10 milliseconds. Our own implementation agrees with the transformers library's to within ten to the minus 5.
8d2b7a66ca50.zh: 波形很难读，所以语音模型看的是它的频谱，一片一片地看。<bookmark mark='a'/>把信号切成25毫秒的窗，每10毫秒一个，每个窗用汉宁窗收尾，再做傅里叶变换：这就是短时傅里叶变换，一张频率对时间的图。<bookmark mark='b'/>人耳大致按比例来听音高，所以把频率合并成在梅尔刻度上均匀分布的频带：一千赫以下窄，以上宽。<bookmark mark='c'/>对每个频带的能量取对数，保留最高的八个数量级，就正好是Whisper听到的东西：每10毫秒80个对数梅尔频带。我们自己的实现，和transformers库的结果相差不到10的负5次方。

26466658d410.en: For most of a century digital sound meant samples: the telephone's 64 thousand bits a second, a CD's 1.4 million. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2021 Neil Zeghidour and colleagues at Google learned a codec end to end. SoundStream's encoder turns the wave into seventy-five vectors a second, residual vector quantization turns each into a handful of code numbers, and a decoder turns codes back into a wave, all trained together, with a spectral loss and a GAN's judge. <bookmark mark='b'/> They also dropped quantizer stages at random during training, so one model works at every bitrate. Meta's EnCodec, in 2022, runs from 1.5 to 24 kilobits a second. <bookmark mark='c'/> The tokenizers of today's speech models go lower still: one or two kilobits.
26466658d410.zh: 将近一个世纪里，数字声音就意味着样本：电话每秒六万四千比特，CD每秒一百四十万。<bookmark mark='a'/>2021年，谷歌的尼尔·泽吉杜尔和同事端到端地学出了一个编解码器。SoundStream的编码器把波形变成每秒七十五个向量，残差向量量化把每个向量变成几个编码数字，解码器再把编码变回波形，三者一起训练，用频谱损失加上GAN的判别器。<bookmark mark='b'/>他们还在训练时随机丢掉一些量化级，于是一个模型能工作在每一种码率。Meta在2022年推出的EnCodec，码率从每秒1.5到24千比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>如今语音模型的分词器还要更低：一两千比特。

5dea19e1e991.en: We built a small one, with one simplification. Teaching a network to make a wave takes far more compute than this computer has, so ours codes the picture Whisper reads, the log-mel spectrogram of chapter eight, and leaves turning a picture back into sound to a vocoder. <bookmark mark='a'/> A strided convolution takes the picture's 100 frames a second down to 50. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each frame passes through up to eight residual stages of 256 codes, eight bits each, so a stage costs 400 bits a second. <bookmark mark='c'/> Stages are dropped at random in training, so the same model runs at 400, 800, 1600 or 3,200 bits a second. <bookmark mark='d'/> It has 1.3 million parameters and trained for 1,500 steps on 6 minutes of Kokoro speech in ten voices, with a plain loss: the average error in the rebuilt picture. Here it learns to rebuild a sentence from a voice it never heard.
5dea19e1e991.zh: 我们自己搭了一个小的，做了一处简化。教一个网络造出波形，需要的算力远超这台电脑，所以我们的编解码器编码的是Whisper读的那张图，也就是第8章的对数梅尔频谱，把图变回声音的事留给声码器。<bookmark mark='a'/>一层带步长的卷积，把这张图每秒100帧降到每秒50帧。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一帧最多经过八级残差量化，每级256个码，八比特，所以一级每秒花400比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>训练时随机丢掉量化级，于是同一个模型可以跑在每秒400, 800, 1600或3200比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>它有1.3百万个参数，在十个声音、6分钟的Kokoro语音上训练了1500步，损失很朴素：重建出的图的平均误差。这是它学着重建一个从没听过的声音说的一句话。

2e36307ca9c5.en: How good is it? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the held-out sentence rebuilt at each bitrate: one stage keeps the rough shape, eight keep much more of the detail. <bookmark mark='b'/> A blunt but fair test: Whisper reads such pictures directly, so can it still understand ours? On 12 held-out sentences, Whisper's word error rate falls from 30 percent at 400 bits a second to 15 percent at 3,200, against 12 percent on the original picture; two seeds. <bookmark mark='c'/> At 3,200 bits a second the codes are 80 times smaller than the picture stored as 32-bit numbers, and 80 times smaller than the samples themselves. A real codec must also make the wave, with a GAN's judge, far more data and far more steps; ours only has to show the trade.
2e36307ca9c5.zh: 它有多好？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是那句留出的话在各个码率下的重建：一级保留了大致的形状，八级保留了多得多的细节。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个粗糙但公平的测试：Whisper直接读这样的图，那它还能听懂我们重建的图吗？在12句留出的话上，Whisper的词错误率下降，从每秒400比特时的30%，到每秒3200比特时的15%，原始的图是12%；两个种子。<bookmark mark='c'/>在每秒3200比特时，这些编码只有用32位数存储那张图的80分之一，是样本本身的80分之一。真正的编解码器还得造出波形，要用判别器、多得多的数据和多得多的步数；我们这个只是要把这种取舍展示出来。

9e09575e2b09.en: Speech tokens come in two kinds. <bookmark mark='a'/> A codec's acoustic tokens carry how the speech sounds: the voice, the room, the detail. Our codec uses its stages fairly evenly: perplexities from 166 to 227 of 256. <bookmark mark='b'/> Semantic tokens carry what is said, and they come from a self-supervised speech model, the kind Part 24 builds, clustered into codes. In 2022 Google's AudioLM generated speech by writing semantic tokens first and acoustic tokens after them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the two were merged into one codec: Kyutai's Mimi teaches its first codebook to match the self-supervised model WavLM, and keeps seven acoustic stages beside it, at 12.5 frames a second and 1.1 kilobits. The narrator's own tokenizer, Qwen3-TTS's, does the same with sixteen.
9e09575e2b09.zh: 语音词元有两种。<bookmark mark='a'/>编解码器的声学词元，携带的是听起来怎样：嗓音、房间、细节。我们的编解码器各级用得相当均匀：困惑度从166到227，满分256。<bookmark mark='b'/>语义词元携带的是说了什么，它们来自一个自监督的语音模型，也就是第24部分要搭的那类模型，再聚类成编码。2022年，谷歌的AudioLM生成语音时，先写语义词元，再写声学词元。<bookmark mark='c'/>后来两者合进了一个编解码器：Kyutai的Mimi教它的第一本码本去对齐自监督模型WavLM，旁边再保留七级声学码，每秒12.5帧，1.1千比特。旁白自己的分词器，Qwen3-TTS的那个，也是这样做的，用十六级。

cac213cbf8ca.en: Chapter ten. From Audrey to hidden Markov models.
cac213cbf8ca.zh: 第10章。从Audrey到隐马尔可夫模型。

6652b1804246.en: Speech recognition began with digits. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1952 three engineers at Bell Labs built Audrey. It split the sound into two frequency bands, tracked each band's frequency by counting how often the signal crossed zero, and compared the pattern with a stored one for each of the ten digits. For the speaker it was tuned to, it was right ninety-seven to ninety-nine times in a hundred; for anyone else it had to be adjusted. <bookmark mark='b'/> We built the same idea: ten templates from one Kokoro voice, one take of each digit, and each new word goes to the nearest template. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same voice, saying the digits again a little faster: 90 percent right. Eleven other voices: 63 percent. The problem of speech recognition was never the words. It was the voices.
6652b1804246.zh: 语音识别是从数字开始的。<bookmark mark='a'/>1952年，贝尔实验室的三位工程师造出了Audrey。它把声音分成两个频带，通过数信号穿过零点的次数来跟踪每个频带的频率，再把这个模式和十个数字各自存好的模式相比。对调好的那个说话人，它一百次里对九十七到九十九次；换了别人，就得重新调。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们做了同样的事：用一个Kokoro声音、每个数字一遍，做出十个模板，每个新词就归到最近的模板。<bookmark mark='c'/>同一个声音，稍快地再说一遍这些数字：对90%。另外十一个声音：63%。语音识别的难题从来不是词，而是声音。

32c2ec665625.en: People say the same word fast or slow, stretching some sounds and not others, so squeezing every word to one length is crude. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1968 Taras Vintsyuk in Kyiv, and in 1978 Hiroaki Sakoe and Seibi Chiba at NEC, aligned the two by dynamic programming: dynamic time warping. The cheapest alignment to each pair of frames extends the cheapest alignment to one of three neighbours. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is the path that matches a new take of seven to the template. <bookmark mark='c'/> Warping helps: 100 percent for the same voice, 74 for the others. And with templates from ten voices, two voices it has never heard get 95 percent. More examples beat cleverer matching, a lesson the field would learn again and again.
32c2ec665625.zh: 人们说同一个词可快可慢，有的音拉长、有的不拉长，所以把每个词都压成同一长度很粗糙。<bookmark mark='a'/>1968年基辅的塔拉斯·温秋克，和1978年NEC的迫江博昭与千叶成美，用动态规划把两者对齐：动态时间规整。到每一对帧的最便宜对齐，是从三个邻居之一的最便宜对齐延伸过来的。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是把seven的一次新录音对齐到模板上的路径。<bookmark mark='c'/>时间规整有帮助：同一个声音100%，其他声音74%。用十个声音的模板，两个从没听过的声音能达到95%。更多的例子胜过更聪明的匹配，这个领域会一次又一次学到这一课。

e0665064f6f5.en: From the mid-1970s, at Carnegie Mellon and at IBM, recognition became statistics. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each word is a hidden Markov model, Part 7's model: a chain of states, one for each sound, that the speech walks through, lingering or moving on. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each state scores the spectrum of a frame with a mixture of Gaussians, all of it trained by EM and decoded by Viterbi. <bookmark mark='c'/> And words are chosen by Bayes' rule: the transcript that best explains the sound, times what a language model expects. That recipe, scaled up, ran dictation and telephone systems for thirty years. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2012 four labs reported together that deep networks beat the Gaussian mixtures as the model of sound. The next question was whether a network could learn the whole thing, without being told which frame is which sound.
e0665064f6f5.zh: 从1970年代中期起，在卡内基梅隆大学和IBM，识别变成了统计。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个词是一个隐马尔可夫模型，第7部分的模型：一串状态，每个音一个，语音沿着它们走过去，或停留，或前进。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个状态用一个高斯混合给一帧的频谱打分，整个模型用EM训练，用维特比解码。<bookmark mark='c'/>词则按贝叶斯法则来选：最能解释这段声音的转写，乘以语言模型对它的预期。这套配方规模化之后，支撑听写和电话系统长达三十年。<bookmark mark='d'/>2012年，四个实验室联合报告：作为声音模型，深度网络胜过了高斯混合。接下来的问题是，一个网络能不能学会整件事，而不用告诉它哪一帧是哪个音。

af201438c775.en: A recognizer hears a hundred frames of sound for a dozen letters, and training data says only what was said, not when. The old systems needed each frame labelled, from a previous model. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2006 Alex Graves, Santiago Fernández, Faustino Gomez and Jürgen Schmidhuber found a way around it. The network outputs, for every frame, a probability for each letter and for one extra symbol, a blank. <bookmark mark='b'/> Any path through the frames becomes text by merging repeated symbols and then dropping the blanks. <bookmark mark='c'/> A blank is also how a real double letter survives: without one between them, the two e's of three merge into one. <bookmark mark='d'/> The probability of the text is the sum over every path that becomes it.
af201438c775.zh: 识别器听到一百帧声音，对应十几个字母，而训练数据只说了说的是什么，没说什么时候说的。旧系统需要每一帧都有标签，从之前的模型得来。<bookmark mark='a'/>2006年，亚历克斯·格雷夫斯、圣地亚哥·费尔南德斯、福斯蒂诺·戈麦斯和于尔根·施密德胡伯找到了绕过去的办法。网络对每一帧，给每个字母一个概率，再加一个额外的符号：空白符。<bookmark mark='b'/>穿过各帧的任何一条路径，先合并重复的符号，再去掉空白符，就变成文本。<bookmark mark='c'/>空白符也是真正的双写字母得以保留的办法：中间没有空白符，three里的两个e就会合成一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>文本的概率，就是所有能变成它的路径之和。

225bf26a6ec4.en: There are exponentially many paths, but the sum is cheap. <bookmark mark='a'/> Write the transcript with a blank before, between and after its letters: two L plus one states, in order. <bookmark mark='b'/> A path at state s at time t was, one frame earlier, at s, or at the state just before. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it may also skip a blank, jumping from two states back, unless that would merge two equal letters. Multiply by the network's probability for the symbol at s. <bookmark mark='d'/> The paths that end on the last letter or the final blank add up to the transcript's probability. <bookmark mark='e'/> It is the forward algorithm of Part 7's hidden Markov models, with the transcript as the chain of states, and minus its logarithm is a loss whose gradient comes from the same recursion run backward.
225bf26a6ec4.zh: 路径的数目是指数级的，但求和很便宜。<bookmark mark='a'/>把转写写出来，在字母前、中间和后面都加上空白符：一共2L加1个状态，按顺序排好。<bookmark mark='b'/>在时刻t处于状态s的路径，前一帧要么在s，要么在它前面的那个状态。<bookmark mark='c'/>它还可以跳过一个空白符，从往回两个状态跳过来，除非那样会把两个相同的字母合并。再乘以网络在这一帧给状态s的符号的概率。<bookmark mark='d'/>结束在最后一个字母或最后一个空白符上的路径，加起来就是转写的概率。<bookmark mark='e'/>这正是第7部分隐马尔可夫模型的前向算法，把转写当作状态链；它的对数取负就是损失，梯度来自同一个递推的反向运行。

2e574245f68d.en: We trained a small recognizer this way: 162 thousand parameters in seven convolutions, on digit strings spoken by ten Kokoro voices, three seeds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is what it hears in a string from a voice it never heard, as training goes on. At first every frame is a blur. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the blank takes over, the cheapest way to be right about most frames. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then letters appear between the blanks: at the end the blank wins 59 percent of the frames, and a letter lasts 4.5 frames on average, CTC's famously peaky alignments. The greedy reading below takes the likeliest symbol at each frame, then merges and drops.
2e574245f68d.zh: 我们用这种方法训练了一个小识别器：162千个参数，七层卷积，用十个Kokoro声音说的数字串训练，三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是在训练过程中，它从一个从没听过的声音说的数字串里听到的东西。起初每一帧都是一片模糊。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后空白符占了上风，这是在大多数帧上答对的最便宜的办法。<bookmark mark='c'/>接着字母出现了，夹在空白符之间：到最后，空白符赢下59%的帧，一个字母平均持续4.5帧，这就是CTC出了名的尖峰式对齐。下面的贪心读法，在每一帧取最可能的符号，再合并、去空白。

f356093c6506.en: And here is the lattice itself, computed from the trained network: the states of the transcript down the side, the frames across. <bookmark mark='a'/> The brightness is how likely each state is at each frame, from the forward and backward passes together; the white line is the single best path. <bookmark mark='b'/> The forward algorithm's total, -3.26 in natural log, agrees with PyTorch's own CTC loss. <bookmark mark='c'/> Averaged over three seeds: 44.8 percent of the digit words wrong for the two new voices, from 32 to 69 depending on the seed, and 9.4 percent for voices it trained on; new voices are much harder than the ones it heard, Audrey's lesson again. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2014 Baidu's Deep Speech trained CTC on thousands of hours and did without the old pipeline. CTC treats each frame's letter as independent of the others, so later systems, RNN transducers and attention-based recognizers, let each letter depend on the ones before.
f356093c6506.zh: 这就是格本身，由训练好的网络算出：转写的各个状态竖着排，各帧横着排。<bookmark mark='a'/>亮度表示每个状态在每一帧上的可能性，由前向和后向两遍合起来得到；白线是唯一的最佳路径。<bookmark mark='b'/>前向算法算出的总和，自然对数为-3.26，与PyTorch自己的CTC损失一致。<bookmark mark='c'/>三个种子平均：两个新声音的数字词错了44.8%，随种子不同从32%到69%不等，训练用过的声音错了9.4%；新声音比它听过的难得多，又是Audrey的那一课。<bookmark mark='d'/>2014年，百度的Deep Speech用几千小时的数据训练CTC，抛开了旧的流水线。CTC把每一帧的字母当作彼此独立，所以后来的系统，RNN转录器和基于注意力的识别器，让每个字母依赖于前面的字母。

cdd9efb255f3.en: After Deep Speech, two roads led to the recognizers we use today. <bookmark mark='a'/> One was self-supervision. Facebook's wav2vec 2.0, in 2020, hid stretches of speech from its own transformer and learned to pick the true hidden frame out of distractors, Part 24's contrastive loss applied to sound. Pretrained on 53,000 hours with no transcripts, then fine-tuned on just ten minutes with them, it got 4.8 and 8.2 percent of the words wrong on the two halves of a standard benchmark. <bookmark mark='b'/> The other road was weak supervision. In December 2022 OpenAI's Whisper trained on 680,000 hours of audio paired with transcripts found on the web, imperfect ones and all, one model that transcribes, translates, names the language and times the words, in nearly a hundred languages.
cdd9efb255f3.zh: Deep Speech之后，有两条路通向我们今天用的识别器。<bookmark mark='a'/>一条是自监督。Facebook在2020年的wav2vec 2.0，把语音的几段藏起来，不让它自己的Transformer看到，再学着从干扰项里挑出真正被藏起来的那一帧，这是把第24部分的对比损失用在声音上。它先在五万三千小时没有转写的语音上预训练，再只用十分钟有转写的语音微调，在一个标准基准的两半上，词错误率分别是4.8%和8.2%。<bookmark mark='b'/>另一条路是弱监督。2022年12月，OpenAI的Whisper在六十八万小时、配有网上找来的转写的音频上训练，不完美的转写也照收；一个模型就能转写、翻译、识别语言、给词标时间，覆盖将近一百种语言。

51684fdf779b.en: Whisper is a plain encoder-decoder transformer, the shape of Part 14's translation model. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its input is chapter eight's picture: 80 log-mel bands every ten milliseconds, always thirty seconds long, padded with silence. <bookmark mark='b'/> The encoder reads it; the decoder writes the transcript one token at a time, with GPT-2's byte-level BPE, attending back to the sound. <bookmark mark='c'/> Special tokens at the start say what to do: here, start of transcript, no timestamps. A recognizer has become a language model that listens. <bookmark mark='d'/> We ran the smallest English model, base.en, 73 million parameters, from the Hugging Face cache.
51684fdf779b.zh: Whisper是一个朴素的编码器-解码器Transformer，和第14部分那个翻译模型同一个形状。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的输入就是第8章那张图：每十毫秒80个对数梅尔频带，永远是三十秒，不够就用静音补齐。<bookmark mark='b'/>编码器读它；解码器用GPT-2的字节级BPE，一次一个词元地写出转写，同时回头关注声音。<bookmark mark='c'/>开头的特殊词元说明要做什么：这里是转写开始，不要时间戳。识别器变成了一个会听的语言模型。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们跑的是最小的英语模型base.en，73百万个参数，来自Hugging Face缓存。

58d4272f4b7d.en: How does it do on our voices? <bookmark mark='a'/> On 24 sentences from the two held-out Kokoro voices, it gets 7.9 percent of the words wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the 40 digit strings, 5.0 percent, counting its numerals as words, against 44.8 for our CTC recognizer, trained on nothing but digits: Whisper does better even on our model's own task. <bookmark mark='c'/> Look at its mistakes: where the sound leaves room, the decoder, a language model, writes what it finds likelier, a plural, a number in figures, two words run together.
58d4272f4b7d.zh: 它在我们的声音上表现如何？<bookmark mark='a'/>在两个留出的Kokoro声音说的24句话上，它的词错误率是7.9%。<bookmark mark='b'/>在40个数字串上是5.0%，把它写出的阿拉伯数字也算作词；我们只用数字训练的CTC识别器是44.8%：即使在我们模型自己的任务上，Whisper也做得更好。<bookmark mark='c'/>看看它的错误：在声音留有余地的地方，解码器这个语言模型，就写下它觉得更可能的东西：一个复数，一个写成阿拉伯数字的数，两个连在一起的词。

371c99711d8f.en: Recognizers kept growing and getting faster: Whisper large-v3 in 2023, and a turbo version that cut its decoder from 32 layers to 4. <bookmark mark='a'/> In January 2026 Alibaba's Qwen3-ASR, built on an omni model, covered 52 languages and dialects. <bookmark mark='b'/> It also works on this series. Every sentence the narrator speaks is transcribed by Qwen3-ASR and spoken again if the transcript doesn't match the script, and a forced aligner times each word, which is how the animations know when to move.
371c99711d8f.zh: 识别器越来越大，也越来越快：2023年的Whisper large-v3，以及一个把解码器从32层砍到4层的加速版。<bookmark mark='a'/>2026年1月，阿里巴巴的Qwen3-ASR建在一个全模态模型之上，覆盖52种语言和方言。<bookmark mark='b'/>它也在为这个系列工作。旁白说的每一句话，都由Qwen3-ASR转写，如果转写和稿子对不上就重说一遍；再由一个强制对齐器给每个词标出时间，动画就是这样知道什么时候该动的。

14c4739ad9b7.en: Speaking is the inverse problem, and it is older than listening. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1939 Bell Labs showed the Voder at the World's Fair: an operator played speech on keys and a pedal. The idea behind it is the voice as a source and a filter: the vocal folds buzz, and the throat and mouth shape the buzz with resonances, the formants. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1980 Dennis Klatt's formant synthesizer computed those resonances from rules; the voice Stephen Hawking used grew out of his work. <bookmark mark='c'/> The robotic edge went away when synthesizers started reusing real recordings: in unit selection, a speaker reads for hours, and the system splices together the pieces that join best. <bookmark mark='d'/> In the 2000s statistical models, hidden Markov models again, predicted the spectrum instead, smooth but muffled.
14c4739ad9b7.zh: 说话是反过来的问题，而且比听更早。<bookmark mark='a'/>1939年，贝尔实验室在世界博览会上展示了Voder：一位操作员用琴键和踏板弹出语音。它背后的想法，是把嗓音看成一个声源加一个滤波器：声带嗡嗡振动，喉咙和口腔用共振，也就是共振峰，去塑造这嗡嗡声。<bookmark mark='b'/>1980年，丹尼斯·克拉特的共振峰合成器按规则算出这些共振；史蒂芬·霍金用的那个声音，就是从他的工作里发展出来的。<bookmark mark='c'/>后来合成器开始重用真实录音，机器腔才褪去：在单元选择里，一个人朗读好几个小时，系统再把衔接得最好的片段拼起来。<bookmark mark='d'/>2000年代，统计模型，又是隐马尔可夫模型，改为预测频谱，平滑却发闷。

82c973898baa.en: In 2016 DeepMind's WaveNet threw out the vocoder's rules and generated the wave itself, one sample at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> It is a language model whose tokens are samples: each predicted from all the ones before, sixteen thousand a second, <bookmark mark='b'/> each sample squashed onto 256 levels by a logarithmic mu-law curve, so the vocabulary is small. <bookmark mark='c'/> To see far enough into the past, its convolutions skip by one, two, four and eight samples, doubling the reach with each layer. Listeners preferred it to the best systems of the day, but it was very slow. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google's Tacotron 2 split the job: a sequence-to-sequence network turns text into a mel spectrogram, and WaveNet turns that into sound. Listeners scored it 4.53 out of 5; real recordings scored 4.58.
82c973898baa.zh: 2016年，DeepMind的WaveNet抛开了声码器的规则，直接生成波形，一次一个采样点。<bookmark mark='a'/>它是一个以采样点为词元的语言模型：每个点都由之前所有的点预测，每秒一万六千个，<bookmark mark='b'/>每个采样点用对数形状的μ律曲线压到256个等级上，所以词表很小。<bookmark mark='c'/>为了看得足够远，它的卷积依次跳过一、二、四、八个采样点，每一层把视野加倍。听众更喜欢它，胜过当时最好的系统，但它非常慢。<bookmark mark='d'/>谷歌的Tacotron 2把工作分成两步：一个序列到序列的网络把文本变成梅尔频谱，WaveNet再把它变成声音。听众给它打了4.53分，满分5分；真实录音是4.58分。

7a541fe35feb.en: Then speech synthesis became language modelling, with chapter nine's codec tokens as the words. <bookmark mark='a'/> Microsoft's VALL-E, in January 2023, takes the text and three seconds of someone's voice, written as EnCodec tokens. <bookmark mark='b'/> A transformer continues the voice prompt, writing the first codebook frame by frame; <bookmark mark='c'/> a second one fills in the finer codebooks all at once, and the codec's decoder makes the wave. <bookmark mark='d'/> Trained on sixty thousand hours, it could speak in a voice it had heard for three seconds, the trick that made voice cloning cheap, and that every speech model since has had to reckon with.
7a541fe35feb.zh: 然后，语音合成变成了语言建模，第9章的编解码器词元就是词。<bookmark mark='a'/>微软在2023年1月推出的VALL-E，接收文本，以及某人三秒钟的声音，写成EnCodec词元。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个Transformer接着这段声音提示往下写，逐帧写出第一本码本；<bookmark mark='c'/>另一个一次性补齐更细的各本码本，编解码器的解码器再生成波形。<bookmark mark='d'/>它在六万小时的语音上训练，只听三秒就能用那个声音说话，这个技巧让声音克隆变得廉价，此后的每个语音模型都得面对它。

2fc8a23ca984.en: This series has a narrator of its own. <bookmark mark='a'/> Qwen3-TTS, from Alibaba in January 2026, was trained on over five million hours of speech in ten languages. Its tokenizer is a codec like Mimi: 12.5 frames a second, sixteen codebooks of 2,048, the first taught by a self-supervised model to carry what is said, the other fifteen how it sounds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its transformer writes the first codebook of each frame, a small module predicts the other fifteen, and the first sound comes out after about a tenth of a second. It can clone a voice from three seconds. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here is the 17-second clip it learned its English voice from, as the codes the narrator sees: 208 frames of sixteen codes, 2,200 bits a second. And here is the narrator saying a sentence of this part: 43 frames, sixteen codes each, written by its transformer before a decoder made them into sound. <bookmark mark='d'/> This copy of the video is read by Kokoro-82M. From the Voder's keys to here took eighty-seven years.
2fc8a23ca984.zh: 这个系列有自己的旁白。<bookmark mark='a'/>Qwen3-TTS，阿里巴巴2026年1月发布，在十种语言、五百多万小时的语音上训练。它的分词器是一个像Mimi那样的编解码器：每秒12.5帧，十六本码本，每本2048个码，第一本由一个自监督模型教着去携带说了什么，其余十五本携带听起来怎样。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的Transformer写出每一帧的第一本码，一个小模块预测其余十五本，大约十分之一秒后就发出第一个声音。它只需三秒就能克隆一个声音。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是它学英语声音所用的那段17秒的片段，写成旁白看到的编码：208帧，每帧十六个码，每秒2200比特。这是旁白说出这一部分里的一句话：43帧，每帧十六个码，由它的Transformer写出，再由解码器变成声音。<bookmark mark='d'/>这份视频由Kokoro-82M朗读。从Voder的琴键到这里，走了八十七年。

6734b60a5e8e.en: Chapter fourteen. Matching pictures and words.
6734b60a5e8e.zh: 第14章。让图片和文字配对。

9f4e2e6d301f.en: Pictures met words in two ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> Around 2014 networks learned to caption photos, a vision network feeding a language model that wrote a sentence. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2021 OpenAI's CLIP did something simpler. Two encoders, one for pictures and one for text, trained on four hundred million pictures with their captions from the web, so that matching pairs get similar vectors. It could then classify pictures it was never trained to classify: write each class as a caption, and pick the closest. On ImageNet that scored 76 percent, without a single one of its labels. <bookmark mark='c'/> We trained a small pair on our letters, with captions like bold serif A. Here's a batch: every picture scored against every caption, <bookmark mark='d'/> and the bright diagonal is the right pairs.
9f4e2e6d301f.zh: 图片和文字以两种方式相遇。<bookmark mark='a'/>2014年前后，网络学会了给照片配说明：一个视觉网络喂给一个语言模型，由它写出一句话。<bookmark mark='b'/>2021年，OpenAI的CLIP做了更简单的事。两个编码器，一个读图片，一个读文字，在网上四亿张图片和它们的说明上训练，让配对的两者得到相近的向量。然后它就能给从没训练过的类别分类：把每个类别写成一句说明，挑最接近的那个。在ImageNet上，这样得到76%，一个标签都没用。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们在字母上训练了一对小编码器，说明像“bold serif A”这样。这是一批数据：每张图片和每句说明都打了分，<bookmark mark='d'/>亮的对角线就是正确的配对。

0ce81d2a584d.en: Part 24 showed that this kind of loss measures information. Here is the same fact seen from the critic's side. <bookmark mark='a'/> The loss asks each picture to pick its caption out of N. <bookmark mark='b'/> The best possible score is the log of how much more likely the caption is given the picture than on its own. <bookmark mark='c'/> Put that in, and divide through by the true pair's term. <bookmark mark='d'/> With many random captions each ratio averages one, and what is left is at least log N minus the mutual information between pictures and words. So log N minus the loss estimates that information from below, and can never exceed log N. <bookmark mark='e'/> Measured on our model with 16, 64 and 256 candidates, three seeds: the estimate grows from 2.62 nats to 4.46, pinned under log N, while the captions themselves hold 6.09. The ceiling belongs to the measurement: with 256 candidates, models trained on batches of 16 and of 256 score 4.43 and 4.46.
0ce81d2a584d.zh: 第24部分说明了这类损失在度量信息。这里从打分函数的角度再看一次。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个损失要求每张图片从N句说明里挑出自己的那句。<bookmark mark='b'/>最好的分数，是给定图片时这句说明的可能性比它单独出现时高多少倍，再取对数。<bookmark mark='c'/>代进去，分子分母同除以真正配对那一项。<bookmark mark='d'/>随机说明很多时，每个比值平均为一，剩下的至少是log N减去图片和文字之间的互信息。所以log N减去损失，是这份信息的一个下界，而且永远超不过log N。<bookmark mark='e'/>在我们的模型上，分别用16、64和256个候选来测，三个种子：估计值从2.62奈特涨到4.46，被压在log N之下，而说明本身含有6.09奈特。这个上限属于测量本身：用256个候选来测时，用16和256的批训练出来的模型，得分分别是4.43和4.46。

745123c9bd7d.en: Here is that table while the two encoders learn. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the start every score is noise. Each batch pulls the matching pairs' vectors together and pushes the others apart, and the diagonal lights up; pairs that share a letter or a style stay partly lit, because they really are alike. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now the test CLIP was famous for. We hid 78 of the 520 captions, every picture of bold mono Q and the like, from training altogether. <bookmark mark='c'/> Asked to choose among all 520 captions, those pictures find their exact caption 55 percent of the time, because the caption encoder learned bold, mono and Q separately, and can put them together.
745123c9bd7d.zh: 这是两个编码器学习时的那张表。<bookmark mark='a'/>一开始，每个分数都是噪声。每一批数据把配对的向量拉近，把其余的推开，对角线就亮了起来；共享一个字母或一种字体的配对仍有几分亮，因为它们本来就相像。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在来做CLIP出名的那个测试。我们把520句说明里的78句，比如“bold mono Q”这样的每一张图片，完全不放进训练。<bookmark mark='c'/>让它在全部520句说明里挑，这些图片有55%找到了完全正确的说明，因为说明编码器分别学会了bold、mono和Q，能把它们组合起来。

9b44969859b9.en: In 2023 Xiaohua Zhai and colleagues at Google changed one thing. CLIP's loss is a softmax over the batch: each picture's score depends on every other caption in it, so the whole batch must be gathered on every chip. <bookmark mark='a'/> SigLIP asks each picture-caption pair a yes-or-no question instead, with a sigmoid and a learned bias. No batch-wide sum, so it scales to enormous batches, and they found it better at small ones. <bookmark mark='b'/> We ran both at three batch sizes, on the same budget of pairs, three seeds each. On the unseen captions, the seeds overlap at the smallest batch, and they overlap at the largest: 53 against 50 percent at 16, 55 against 57 at 256, CLIP first. <bookmark mark='c'/> At scale, SigLIP's encoders became the eyes of many open vision-language models.
9b44969859b9.zh: 2023年，谷歌的翟晓华和同事只改了一处。CLIP的损失是对整批数据做softmax：每张图片的分数取决于批里的每一句说明，所以整批数据必须收集到每块芯片上。<bookmark mark='a'/>SigLIP改为对每一对图片和说明问一个是或否的问题，用sigmoid加一个学出来的偏置。没有整批的求和，所以能扩展到极大的批，而他们发现它在小批上也更好。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们在三种批大小下训练了两者，同样的配对总数，各三个种子。在没见过的说明上，最小的批上各种子的结果互相重叠，最大的批上也互相重叠：批大小16时53%对50%，256时55%对57%，CLIP在前。<bookmark mark='c'/>在大规模上，SigLIP的编码器成了许多开源视觉语言模型的眼睛。

71ab518d3ac7.en: CLIP matches pictures with captions, but it can't answer a question about a picture. For that, connect a vision encoder to a language model. <bookmark mark='a'/> DeepMind's Flamingo, in 2022, squeezed each picture into 64 tokens and added new cross-attention layers to a frozen language model. <bookmark mark='b'/> Salesforce's BLIP-2 sent 32 learned queries to a frozen image encoder. <bookmark mark='c'/> And in April 2023 LLaVA showed how little it takes: a single linear map turns each of CLIP's patch vectors into a vector in the language model's word space, and the picture is just more tokens at the start of the prompt. <bookmark mark='d'/> Train the map on captions, then fine-tune on 158 thousand examples of chat about pictures that GPT-4 wrote from their captions. Nearly every open vision-language model since has this shape.
71ab518d3ac7.zh: CLIP能给图片配说明，却回答不了关于一张图片的问题。要做到这一点，得把一个视觉编码器接到语言模型上。<bookmark mark='a'/>DeepMind在2022年的Flamingo，把每张图片压成64个词元，并给一个冻结的语言模型加上新的交叉注意力层。<bookmark mark='b'/>Salesforce的BLIP-2向一个冻结的图像编码器发出32个学出来的查询。<bookmark mark='c'/>2023年4月，LLaVA表明需要的东西少得惊人：一个线性映射，把CLIP的每个小块向量变成语言模型词空间里的一个向量，图片就只是提示开头多出来的一些词元。<bookmark mark='d'/>先在说明文字上训练这个映射，再用GPT-4根据图片说明写出的十五万八千条关于图片的对话样例来微调。此后几乎每个开源视觉语言模型都是这个样子。

ba9053f9addb.en: Early models resized every picture to one small square, 224 or 336 pixels on a side. That's fine for a dog, fatal for a receipt. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our letter-reading CLIP shows the effect: shrink its twenty-pixel letters and blow them back up. At ten pixels it still reads 88 percent of the letters; at five, 42. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2024 Qwen2-VL stopped resizing to a square. A picture keeps roughly its own size and shape, is cut into 14-pixel patches, and every two by two patches become one token, so a small icon costs a few dozen tokens and a big screenshot over a thousand. These counts come from the published code.
ba9053f9addb.zh: 早期的模型把每张图片都缩成一个小正方形，边长224或336像素。拍一只狗没问题，拍一张收据就完了。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们那个读字母的CLIP能说明这种效果：把它二十像素的字母缩小，再放大回去。十像素时，它仍能读对88%的字母；五像素时，只有42%。<bookmark mark='b'/>2024年，Qwen2-VL不再缩成正方形。一张图片大致保持自己的大小和形状，切成14像素的小块，每二乘二个小块合成一个词元，于是一个小图标花几十个词元，一张大截图要一千多个。这些数字来自公开的代码。

ca432acea20a.en: A picture's tokens are a grid, not a line, and positions should say so. <bookmark mark='a'/> Qwen2-VL's answer, M-RoPE, gives every token three coordinates: time, row and column. Text tokens use the same number three times, so for text it is ordinary RoPE from Part 13. <bookmark mark='b'/> A picture's tokens share one time and take their own rows and columns, and the text after it carries on past the largest number used. <bookmark mark='c'/> The rotary dimensions are split three ways, each part rotated by one coordinate, so attention can tell neighbours in the picture from neighbours in the sentence. <bookmark mark='d'/> Video adds frames in time; Qwen2.5-VL tied that axis to real seconds, and Qwen3-VL spread the three across the frequencies.
ca432acea20a.zh: 一张图片的词元是一个网格，而不是一条线，位置编码应该体现这一点。<bookmark mark='a'/>Qwen2-VL的答案M-RoPE，给每个词元三个坐标：时间、行和列。文本词元三个坐标都用同一个数，所以对文本来说，它就是第13部分普通的RoPE。<bookmark mark='b'/>一张图片的词元共用一个时间，各取自己的行和列，而图片后面的文本从用过的最大数字之后接着数。<bookmark mark='c'/>旋转的维度分成三份，每份按一个坐标旋转，这样注意力就能分清图片里的邻居和句子里的邻居。<bookmark mark='d'/>视频在时间上多出了帧；Qwen2.5-VL把这根轴和真实的秒数挂钩，Qwen3-VL把三个坐标交错铺到各个频率上。

9f78146c13e7.en: The connector recipe bolts a vision encoder onto a model that learned language alone. <bookmark mark='a'/> The newer recipe trains on mixed sequences from the start, early fusion. In 2024 Meta's Chameleon wrote pictures as VQ tokens in the same vocabulary as words, Part 22's image tokens. <bookmark mark='b'/> In February 2026 Alibaba's Qwen3.5 was trained from the start on text and picture tokens together; by its model card it matches its text-only predecessor on text and beats the dedicated vision-language models on pictures. Seeing is no longer an add-on.
9f78146c13e7.zh: 连接器的做法，是把一个视觉编码器硬接到一个只学过语言的模型上。<bookmark mark='a'/>更新的做法是从一开始就在混合序列上训练，也就是早期融合。2024年，Meta的Chameleon把图片写成VQ词元，和词放在同一个词表里，也就是第22部分的图像词元。<bookmark mark='b'/>2026年2月，阿里巴巴的Qwen3.5从一开始就在文本和图片词元上一起训练；据它的模型卡，它在文本上和只做文本的前代相当，在图片上胜过专门的视觉语言模型。看，已经不再是一个附加功能了。

b6663afe0913.en: Chapter sixteen. Every sense at once.

ad39c079c96a.en: The voice assistants of the 2010s were cascades: <bookmark mark='a'/> a recognizer turned your speech into text, a language model wrote a reply, and a synthesizer read it out. Each stage waits for the one before, and everything the text can't hold, the tone, the laugh, the hesitation, is lost on the way. <bookmark mark='b'/> In May 2024 OpenAI's GPT-4o put it all in one network trained end to end on text, pictures and sound, answering speech in as little as 232 milliseconds, 320 on average, about as fast as people take turns.
ad39c079c96a.zh: 2010年代的语音助手是级联的：<bookmark mark='a'/>一个识别器把你的话变成文字，一个语言模型写出回复，一个合成器再把它读出来。每一级都要等上一级，而文字装不下的东西，语气、笑声、迟疑，一路上都丢了。<bookmark mark='b'/>2024年5月，OpenAI的GPT-4o把这一切放进一个网络，在文本、图片和声音上端到端训练，回应语音最快只要232毫秒，平均320毫秒，和人们轮流说话的速度差不多。

ba66dcda6f6b.en: GPT-4o still took turns. Conversation doesn't: people interrupt, overlap and murmur mm-hm while the other one talks. <bookmark mark='a'/> In September 2024 Kyutai's Moshi modelled two streams of sound at once, the user's and its own, eighty milliseconds at a time, so it is always listening, even while it speaks. <bookmark mark='b'/> Alongside its own speech it writes the words it is saying, slightly ahead of the sound, an inner monologue that keeps the speech on track. Its latency: 160 milliseconds in theory, about 200 in practice.
ba66dcda6f6b.zh: GPT-4o还是一轮一轮地说。真正的对话不是这样：人们会打断、会重叠，会在对方说话时嗯嗯应和。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年9月，Kyutai的Moshi同时建模两条声音流，用户的和它自己的，每次八十毫秒，所以它一直在听，即使在说话的时候。<bookmark mark='b'/>在自己的语音旁边，它还写下自己正在说的词，比声音稍稍提前，这段内心独白让语音不跑偏。它的延迟：理论上160毫秒，实际上大约200毫秒。

8421c37dc006.en: Alibaba's open omni models split the work in two. <bookmark mark='a'/> A Thinker, a language model, reads one sequence of text, picture and sound tokens, with rotary positions aligned by time, and writes text. <bookmark mark='b'/> A smaller Talker writes speech codes as it goes, and a decoder turns them into sound; in Qwen3-Omni, twelve and a half frames a second through a small convolutional decoder. In Qwen2.5-Omni the Talker read the Thinker's hidden states; in Qwen3-Omni it reads only the words and the sound and picture features, so tools and safety filters can step in on the text before it is spoken. <bookmark mark='c'/> Qwen3-Omni, in September 2025, made both halves mixtures of experts and released the weights; Qwen3.5-Omni, in April 2026, holds more than ten hours of audio in one context. And NVIDIA's PersonaPlex, in January 2026, carried full-duplex talk forward with a voice and a role to play.
8421c37dc006.zh: 阿里巴巴的开源全模态模型把工作一分为二。<bookmark mark='a'/>思考者是一个语言模型，读一串由文本、图片和声音词元组成的序列，旋转位置按时间对齐，写出文本。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个更小的说话者边走边写出语音编码，再由解码器变成声音；在Qwen3-Omni里，是每秒十二帧半，经过一个小的卷积解码器。在Qwen2.5-Omni里，说话者读的是思考者的隐藏状态；在Qwen3-Omni里，它只读词，以及声音和图片的特征，这样工具和安全过滤器就能在文本被说出来之前介入。<bookmark mark='c'/>2025年9月的Qwen3-Omni，把两半都做成了混合专家，并公开了权重；2026年4月的Qwen3.5-Omni，一个上下文里能装下十多个小时的音频。而NVIDIA在2026年1月推出的PersonaPlex，把全双工对话又往前推了一步，可以指定一个声音和一个要扮演的角色。

e83a05128e5d.en: In the end, every sense is a stream of tokens, and what differs is how many. <bookmark mark='a'/> The words of speech come at about 6 tokens a second, by Whisper's own tokenizer on our voices. <bookmark mark='b'/> The same speech as Mimi's codes is 100 a second, as the narrator's tokenizer 200, and a single high-definition frame of video is 1,196 tokens. <bookmark mark='c'/> A minute of conversation is 6,000 tokens per stream at Mimi's rate, so much of the engineering in these models is in spending fewer: lower frame rates, fewer codebooks, smaller pictures where they will do.
e83a05128e5d.zh: 说到底，每一种感官都是一串词元，区别在于有多少。<bookmark mark='a'/>按Whisper自己的分词器、在我们的声音上量，语音里的词大约每秒6个词元。<bookmark mark='b'/>同样的语音写成Mimi的编码是每秒100个，写成旁白的分词器是200个，而一帧高清视频就是1196个词元。<bookmark mark='c'/>按Mimi的速率，一分钟的对话每条流就有6000个词元，所以这些模型里很多工程都花在少用词元上：更低的帧率，更少的码本，能用小图时就用小图。

b5a5baa57c77.en: Let's take stock. Byte-pair encoding cuts text by merging the commonest pairs, a greedy compressor; the unigram model puts a probability on every cut; and bits per character is the fair way to compare them. Bytes and entropy patches spend a model's effort where the surprise is. Pictures and sound become tokens through codebooks, which collapse unless they are restarted, or replaced by a fixed grid, and residual stages make codecs that carry speech in a few hundred bits a second. Sampling folds what is too fast back into the band; spectra and the mel scale are what recognizers hear. CTC learns to transcribe without alignments by summing over a lattice, Whisper learns from the web, and speech synthesis became language modelling over codec tokens. Contrastive training puts pictures and words in one space, and with everything as tokens, one model can see, listen and speak at once.
b5a5baa57c77.zh: 我们来盘点一下。字节对编码靠反复合并最常见的对来切分文本，是一个贪心的压缩器；一元模型给每一种切法一个概率；而每字符比特数是比较它们的公平方式。字节和按熵分块，把模型的力气花在意外所在的地方。图片和声音通过码本变成词元，码本若不重启就会坍缩，或者干脆换成固定的网格；残差分级做出的编解码器，每秒几百比特就能装下语音。采样把太快的部分折回频段里；频谱和梅尔刻度是识别器听到的东西。CTC在一张格上求和，不需要对齐就学会转写；Whisper从网上学习；语音合成变成了在编解码器词元上的语言建模。对比训练把图片和文字放进同一个空间，而当一切都是词元，一个模型就能同时看、听、说。

182de5c3e50d.en: All of this comes back. The self-supervised speech and image encoders that semantic tokens and vision-language models are built on are the next part, Part 24. Reasoning models think in tokens, in Part 28. Robots and world models write actions and video frames as tokens, in Part 29. What the tokens come to mean inside a model is Part 30. And the quirks of tokenizers in benchmarks, and voices cloned from three seconds of speech, come back in the last part, on trust.
182de5c3e50d.zh: 这些都会再出现。语义词元和视觉语言模型所依赖的自监督语音和图像编码器，就是下一部分，第24部分。推理模型用词元思考，在第28部分。机器人和世界模型把动作和视频帧写成词元，在第29部分。词元在模型内部最终意味着什么，是第30部分。而分词器在基准测试里的怪癖，以及只用三秒语音克隆出来的声音，会在最后一部分、关于信任的那一部分再出现。

f6d3ab7f4f4d.en: Here are six problems, from counting merges to the information a batch can certify. Pause here, and work through them; full solutions are in this part's notes.
f6d3ab7f4f4d.zh: 这里有六道题，从数合并次数，到一个批次能证实多少信息。在这里暂停一下，把它们做一做；完整的解答在这一部分的笔记里。

b4074e660478.en: Next time: where encoders like wav2vec 2.0 and DINO come from, when nobody labels anything. Two views of one input, pulled together, everything else pushed apart, and the other ways to learn from data alone: learning without labels, Part 24.
b4074e660478.zh: 下一次：在没人打标签的时候，wav2vec 2.0和DINO这样的编码器是从哪里来的。同一个输入的两个视角拉到一起，其余的都推开，以及只从数据本身学习的其他办法：不用标签的学习，第24部分。

aad934b3e039.en: Jurafsky and Martin's Speech and Language Processing is the place to go deeper: tokenization, recognition and synthesis are all in it. Thanks for watching, and see you in Part 24.
aad934b3e039.zh: 想深入学习，可以读朱拉夫斯基和马丁的《语音与语言处理》（Speech and Language Processing）：分词、识别和合成都在里面。感谢观看，第24部分见。
